hook.evidence: 'Did you know honey basically never goes bad?' — the premise is there but phrased with the generic 'Did you know…' the anchor names.

structure.evidence: Setup (tombs) -> explanation (low water, peroxide enzyme, acidity) -> payoff 'That's why your honey jar can sit in the cupboard for years.'; tension stays flat and the last line jumps to a crystallised-honey tip instead of landing or looping.

clarity.evidence: Mostly one idea per sentence and retellable ('honey has very little water in it, so bacteria can't grow'), but the closing line introduces crystallisation, never set up, overloading the end; nearer 5.

pace.evidence: 95 spoken words / 30 s = 3.17 wps, inside 2.0-3.2 but above 2.8; longer lines ('Archaeologists have reported finding pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that were still edible.') are a stretch for one breath; no visual cues.

accuracy.evidence: Claims plausible and the tomb claim is hedged ('have reported'), but no source is given for the water, enzyme or acidity claims.

voice.evidence: Consistent but plain explainer register ('really hard for microbes to survive', 'All of these things together'); no specific wording; between 1 and 3, nearer 3 only for consistency.

notes: Pace counted on all spoken text; item has no bracketed notes.
